Understanding Punctoplasty and Its Importance

Punctoplasty is a surgical procedure designed to widen or open the tear duct punctum (the small openings on the inner corners of the eyelids) to improve tear drainage. Blocked or narrowed tear ducts can lead to excessive tearing, discomfort, and recurrent eye infections. Punctoplasty offers a solution by restoring the natural flow of tears from the eyes to the nasal cavity.

Why Tear Ducts Become Blocked and How Punctoplasty Helps

Tear ducts can become blocked or narrowed due to various reasons, including:

Aging

Natural aging can cause the tear ducts to narrow.

Inflammation

Chronic eye infections or inflammatory conditions can lead to tear duct blockage.

Injury

Trauma to the eye or eyelid can damage the tear ducts.

Congenital Issues

Some individuals are born with narrow or blocked tear ducts.

Punctoplasty involves making a small incision in the punctum to widen the opening, allowing tears to drain more effectively. This procedure can provide significant relief from the symptoms associated with blocked tear ducts.

The Punctoplasty Procedure: What to Expect

Undergoing punctoplasty at AestheticEye is a straightforward and effective process. Here’s what you can expect:

Comprehensive Consultation and Evaluation

During your initial consultation, Dr. Henson or Dr. Pargament will perform a detailed examination of your eyes and tear ducts. They will discuss your symptoms, medical history, and treatment goals to determine if punctoplasty is the right option for you.

Customized Surgical Plan

Based on the evaluation, a personalized surgical plan will be developed. This plan will outline the specifics of the punctoplasty procedure, including the technique to be used and any additional treatments that may be beneficial.

Minimally Invasive Surgery

Punctoplasty is typically performed under local anesthesia, ensuring minimal discomfort. The procedure involves making a small incision in the punctum to widen the tear duct opening. This allows for better tear drainage and alleviates the symptoms of blocked tear ducts.

Post-Operative Care and Recovery

After the procedure, Dr. Henson or Dr. Pargament will provide detailed aftercare instructions to ensure a smooth recovery. Most patients experience minimal discomfort and can return to normal activities within a few days. Follow-up appointments will be scheduled to monitor healing and assess the success of the surgery.

Frequently Asked Questions | Punctoplasty: Tear Duct Repair Surgery

How Do I Know If I Need Punctoplasty?

If you experience persistent excessive tearing, recurrent eye infections, or discomfort due to blocked tear ducts, a consultation with Dr. Henson or Dr. Pargament can determine if punctoplasty is right for you.

What Are the Risks of Punctoplasty?

As with any surgical procedure, there are potential risks, including infection, bleeding, and scarring. However, these risks are minimized when the procedure is performed by experienced surgeons like Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament at AestheticEye.

How Long Does the Punctoplasty Procedure Take?

The punctoplasty procedure typically takes about 30 minutes to an hour, depending on the complexity of the case. Most patients can go home the same day.

Can Punctoplasty Be Combined with Other Procedures?

Yes, punctoplasty can be combined with other eyelid or tear duct procedures if necessary. Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament will discuss all options during your consultation.

Will My Insurance Cover Punctoplasty?

Insurance coverage for punctoplasty varies. If the procedure is deemed medically necessary to address a blocked tear duct, it may be covered. Our team at AestheticEye can help you navigate your insurance options.
